item.title: Investment demand fuels China's gold buying
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Investment demand fuels China's gold buying Households viewing physical bullion as safe-haven asset, store of wealth Shoppers crowd jewelry counters during major Chinese holidays, yet a noticeable shift is unfolding across retail outlets nationwide: sparkling gold ornaments are losing ground to plain gold bars and coins. For ordinary households, gold is evolving from a festive gift or fashion statement into a favored store of household wealth. For Fu Hao, a 35-year-old marketing manager in Beijing, the calculation has entirely changed. While he once purchased intricately designed gold bracelets for family milestones, he now opts for unadorned bullion. "The premiums you pay for jewelry craftsmanship just aren't worth it anymore," Fu said shortly after purchasing a 50-gram investment bar at a local bank. "We want our purchases to hold their pure value. It may not be wearable, but a plain gold bar provides real peace of mind." This retail trend mirrors a far-reaching strategic shift, according to a recent report by S&P Global. Far from a short-term rush, China's growing engagement with gold spans household asset allocation, domestic mining expansion, central bank reserve building, cross-border financial infrastructure, and outbound resource investment — all unfolding against a broader wave of gold accumulation across emerging economies. Chinese buyers are re-prioritizing gold bars and coins over decorative jewelry, with many families now viewing physical gold as an alternative safe-haven asset, according to the industry data released by the China Gold Association. This structural divergence is becoming increasingly pronounced. According to the CGA, China's gold consumption reached 511.41 metric tons in the first half of 2026, up 1.23 percent year-on-year. However, demand for gold jewelry plummeted 33.88 percent to 132.13 tons, while robust investment demand pushed the consumption of gold bars and coins to 339.34 tons, surging 28.42 percent. Periodic price pullbacks have consistently stimulated sales of gold bars through domestic banking channels, cementing them as a popular hedge against market risks. "This demand cannot be suppressed, even with gold prices at historical highs," said Zhao Xiangbin, chief strategist at Beijing Gold and Forex Fortune Investment Management. "Investor anxieties about geopolitical situations and tariff wars have intensified, leading to a gold market rush to balance asset portfolios and hedge against risks," he said. This consumer phenomenon is not unique to China. S&P Global data point to similar patterns across emerging markets: retail investors are cutting spending on ornamental gold while lifting investment-grade gold purchases when geopolitical and domestic economic risks rise.

item.title: Visitors flock to Shaanxi for its natural beauty
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
"The scenery is stunning," Ilia Popov, 25, a Russian pursuing postgraduate studies at a university in Xianyang, Northwest China's Shaanxi province, exclaimed when taking in the majesty of the Ganquan Canyon. "It's like a painter has drawn his brush across the stone." Located in Ganquan county, Yan'an, Shaanxi province, the Ganquan Canyon is a slot canyon tucked away on the Loess Plateau, earning it the nickname of China's equivalent to the Antelope Canyon in Arizona, the United States. Yan'an is also renowned for its Red tourism. Carved from red sandstone over tens of millions of years through wind erosion, water dissolution and scouring, the Ganquan Canyon is a unique kind of landscape, known as a Danxia landform. It consists of more than 120 gorges, each with distinctive features. Among the most well-known is Huashugou Gorge. It stretches about 1,100 meters, soaring to over 20 meters at its highest point, with widths ranging from one to two meters. Its narrowest point at the floor of the gorge is just 20 centimeters. Popov made his way through the gorge — wide at first, before narrowing gradually until, at its deepest point, allowing only one visitor to pass at a time. Back home, he posted the photos on social media, where his friends commented that the scenery looked like a scene straight out of a sci-fi film. The canyon first captured widespread public attention through stunning images shared online by photographers about a decade ago. In 2017, the Ganquan Canyon scenic area was established and opened to the public. It received 38,000 visitors during the recently concluded National Day holiday. No one knows its gorges better than Yan Dong, a 62-year-old photographer based in Xi'an, Shaanxi, who devoted himself to exploring the Ganquan Canyon between 2015 and 2021. Yan recalled that in 2015, several of the gorges were only known among local villagers and photographers, and he resolved to fully explore the canyon. He braved wild conditions, sought guidance from elderly local villagers and plotted his routes on maps. At the peak of his explorations, he visited the site more than 100 times in a single year. He said he had personally explored more than 30 gorges in the Ganquan Canyon — all previously unknown to outsiders — photographed them and published a photography album of his work. "Something seemed to draw me deeper into exploring the canyon, as if I were on a mission," Yan said. The endeavor was not without risks. He suffered several accidents and injuries, but he never gave up. "Every gorge has its own soul. To others, they may look similar, but to me, each one is different, as if they were my own children. Within each gorge, every section and every spot is distinctive, each yielding unique photographic opportunities," Yan said. The most vibrant colors appear at midday, when sunlight streams into the gorges, he said. "If you visit the day after it rains, the moss is greener and the red sandstone takes on an even deeper hue. It looks even more spectacular." Yan added that he is proud to have contributed to local tourism through his photography. For conservation purposes, the scenic area only opens about five of the canyon's gorges to the public, with two gorges available each day depending on weather and other conditions on the day. Wu Wenjing, a tour guide based in Yan'an, said that many tourists sign up for one-day tours that depart from the city's downtown, which is more than 80 kilometers away. She added that as Yan'an was the center of the Communist revolution from 1935 to 1948 and the former home of the headquarters of the Communist Party of China, Red tourism sites are also popular destinations, in addition to other natural scenic spots. Wu noted that facilities and services at the scenic area have improved to accommodate a steady rise in visitors to the Ganquan Canyon in recent years. Contact the writers at xulin@chinadaily.com.cn If you go The Ganquan Canyon scenic area sets an adult ticket price of 168 yuan ($25), which covers admission and a mandatory shuttle bus ride. Visitors can drive to the scenic area from Xi'an or Yan'an, both in Shaanxi province. Alternatively, visitors can take a high-speed train from Xi'an to Ganquan North Railway Station, then take a 40-kilometer taxi ride to the scenic area.

item.title: AI accessibility empowering ordinary people
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
AI accessibility empowering ordinary people Record-breaking Shanghai competition highlights growth of user-friendly coding to prioritize focus on ideas For most children, when summer camp ends, all that remains are photos, journal entries and memories that gradually fade. However, 9-year-old Luo Ange turned a seven-day pottery journey into an online "Clay Lab" that can be accessed and shared at any time. She used an artificial intelligence tool to input natural sentences to help write code and create the online lab, a process known as "vibe coding". Highly praised for its innovative concept, well-thought-out product logic and human touch, the work stood out among over 10,000 competitors to win one of the first prizes at Shanghai's Bund Hackathon AI Coding Competition that ended on Sept 9. Luo's inspiration came from attending a pottery summer camp in the mountains of Ganzhou, Jiangxi province, during the summer holidays. She experienced the entire process of traditional pottery-making, from digging the clay, sifting out impurities, mixing the clay, gathering firewood, loading the kiln, and firing and keeping watch over it. The details sparked an idea. Luo wanted to turn everything she had made, seen and learned into a digital work that can be preserved and shared. After learning about the Bund Hackathon competition, she was encouraged by her father to bring her idea to life. With no coding experience and no existing reference work to consult, she turned to AI tools including ChatGPT and Kimi, using conversational communication and precise requests to build the lab's framework and details. After two days, Luo transformed her concept into an online link. Without the need to download anything or log in, users can simply open their browser to explore the pottery-making experience. The lab faithfully follows the major steps of the pottery-making process, and features social functions such as visiting friends, sending flowers and saving pottery shards. Luo wants her lab to be seen by a large number of viewers and also act as a tribute to the work of the summer camp organizers. She also hopes it will help connect more of her peers. The Clay Lab has no scores, rankings, rewards or punishments, as Luo sees no right or wrong answers in creativity. In her online pottery museum, even pieces that failed to fire properly or are imperfect are on display. It's not the first time Luo tried to use AI for creative work. Through trial and error she learned about communicating, collaborating and iterating with AI, honing her logical thinking and problem-solving skills. "AI is more like a friend I can communicate with and work with. When the AI produces errors or the content is off, I patiently point out the issues, communicate with it and make adjustment to refine it bit by bit," said Luo.

item.title: Road map set for ramping up development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Road map set for ramping up development China has laid out a top-level road map dedicated to accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, which officials and analysts said could better sustain long-term economic expansion as the world's second-largest economy shifts toward new growth drivers. The latest guidelines, jointly released on Friday by the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council, China's Cabinet, place greater emphasis on sci-tech innovation and its closer integration with industry, as well as stronger institutional support. Developing new quality productive forces — a concept first proposed in 2023 — is "an intrinsic requirement and an important focus" of high-quality development, the guidelines say. Authorities have acknowledged emerging challenges in putting the concept into practice, including poorly planned investment, neglect of upgrades to traditional industries and insufficient attention to reform. To keep the process on the right track, the guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old", an official from the National Development and Reform Commission said when elaborating on the document. In line with those principles, the document sets out 19 measures in five areas, with technological innovation topping the agenda. Priorities include strengthening "original and disruptive innovation" and speeding up the commercialization of research findings. Companies are assuming a central role in innovation, with their research and development spending estimated to account for more than 77 percent of China's total in 2025, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. That is close to the level of developed economies. The guidelines seek to further strengthen that role, calling for the establishment of a corporate R&D reserve system and a higher rate of additional tax deductions for R&D expenses. Furthermore, corporate R&D projects that meet national strategic needs will be designated as national projects under established procedures, the guidelines say. Li Chao, chief economist at Zheshang Securities, said he sees room for the additional R&D tax deduction rate for technology companies to rise from 100 percent to 120 percent. The measures mark a major shift from government-led to business-led allocation of innovation resources, said Fu Yifu, a researcher at Jiangsu Su Merchants Bank. As companies assume a greater role in innovation, more targeted government intervention is required to strike the right balance between government and the market, the NDRC official said. Authorities should focus on correcting market failures and ensuring fair competition, while curbing wasteful spending and copycat projects. The push for technological innovation also goes hand in hand with efforts to upgrade China's industrial base. "Developing new quality productive forces involves not only fostering emerging and future industries but also upgrading traditional sectors," the NDRC official said. To that end, the guidelines back companies' use of digital, smart and green technologies to upgrade traditional industries, while seeking to foster new pillar industries and establish mechanisms to sustain investment growth and share risks in future industries. In particular, the document gives priority to advancing the "AI Plus" initiative to expand AI applications across sectors. It also stresses the need to establish systems for technology monitoring, risk alerts and emergency response to ensure that AI is "safe, reliable and controllable". The parallel focus on upgrading traditional industries and fostering new ones points to a more coordinated approach to industrial policy, offering a practical path for China to improve its economic structure while maintaining overall stability, said Fu from Jiangsu Su Merchants Bank. On the institutional front, the guidelines promote patient capital for early-stage technology ventures and support stock market listings by eligible technology companies. Researchers will also face fewer barriers to moving between universities, research institutes and businesses. Greater openness is also a key part of the innovation push, as major economies step up investment in frontier technologies. The guidelines encourage foreign venture capital firms to expand in China and support the development of global innovation networks. For Dekra, a German testing, inspection and certification company, China's advances in AI, digital and green technologies are underpinning its continued expansion in the country, said Kilian Aviles, executive vice-president of the company and head of its Asia-Pacific operations. Dekra has upgraded and expanded key laboratories in Shanghai, Suzhou in Jiangsu province, Guangzhou in Guangdong province and Hefei in Anhui province. China's technological advances are also enabling Dekra to "bring proven solutions developed in China to markets across the Asia-Pacific and beyond", Aviles said.

item.title: Zheng crowned China Open champion in historic triumph
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Zheng crowned China Open champion in historic triumph at home tournament Wild card Zheng Qinwen capped her China Open run with an ace on match point, downing No 4 seed Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 on Sunday night to become the first Chinese player to win the title at her home tournament — and claim her maiden WTA 1000 crown. The 24-year-old fought off three set points to take a tight opening set 7-5, reeling off the last 11 points, before breaking late in the second to seal victory in one hour and 43 minutes and send the National Tennis Center into a frenzy. "I always feel very proud to play in front of my home crowd. I always want to show them my best level, because I know how much they support me," Zheng said. "I don't want to let them down, and at the same time I don't want to let myself down. In a way, it's pressure, but at the same time it gives me motivation. "The feeling was incredible to win here in Beijing, in front of my home crowd. It has been one of my dreams," she said. Andreeva, this year's French Open champion, was gracious in defeat. "For sure, today she played great. We all know that she's had a tough year," said the 19-year-old. "I think that she's going to be raising her level even more soon." The title caps a remarkable turnaround for Zheng, who won China's first Olympic tennis singles gold medal in Paris in 2024 — a standout year in which she reached world No 5 by year-end — before an elbow injury slammed the brakes on her rise the next year. Plagued by injuries, she tumbled to No 160 by June and had not strung together more than two straight wins at any tournament before arriving in New York, where she battled through qualifying and achieved seven wins in a row to storm into the US Open quarterfinals, falling to eventual champion Elena Rybakina on Sept 9. That run featured two stunning comebacks: a 1-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5 upset of 2025 Australian Open champion Madison Keys after trailing 0-5 in the third set, and a 7-5, 6-3 round-of-16 stunner over six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek after bouncing back from 0-5 in the first set. Her US Open resurgence raised home fans' expectations over her performance in China — and her historic win in Beijing delivered on that promise, marking a highlight of a booming Chinese season that includes the Shanghai Masters and the Wuhan Open. Zheng's comeback has also drawn widespread attention, and it drove China Open ticket sales to a record high. Total attendance at the National Tennis Center is projected to exceed 450,000, up 25 percent year-on-year, said Chen Jie, executive deputy director and secretary-general of the China Open Organizing Committee, at a news conference on Sunday. Of those, 60 percent came from outside Beijing and nearly 10,000 from overseas. Single-day attendance surpassed 35,000 for six consecutive days, topping 40,000 on both Oct 1 and 2. Overall ticket revenue reached 132 million yuan ($19.7 million), up 48 percent year-on-year and a record high, while tournament-related consumer spending is expected to exceed 55 million yuan, an increase of 55 percent, Chen added.

item.title: Talks highlight deepening of cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Talks highlight deepening of cooperation The latest China-France Strategic Dialogue has reinforced a long-standing channel for high-level communication and reaffirmed a shared commitment to independence and cooperation at a time of global uncertainty, experts said. Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, participated in the 28th round of the dialogue with the French President's Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne on Saturday in Datong, North China's Shanxi province. The two sides pledged to maintain close high-level exchanges, deepen cooperation in areas such as aerospace and nuclear energy, and broaden cooperation in emerging areas including advanced manufacturing and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthen people-to-people ties. Jian Junbo, director of Fudan University's Center for China-Europe Relations in Shanghai, said the annual dialogue provides continuity in bilateral communication. France's ambition to play a major role in international affairs also gives its strategic engagement with China particular significance, he said. The choice of Datong connected the latest discussions with an earlier chapter in bilateral relations. Georges Pompidou, the first French president to visit China, traveled to the city in 1973, making it his first stop after Beijing, accompanied by then Chinese premier Zhou Enlai. Jin Ling, director of the China Institute of International Studies' Department for Global Governance and International Organizations Studies in Beijing, said that holding the dialogue in Datong reflected a strategic choice by both sides, carrying political symbolism and cultural significance. It embodied the spirit that underpinned the establishment of China-France diplomatic relations — a legacy that remains a distinctive strength of ties and offers an important example for relations between major countries, she said. China and France established diplomatic relations during the Cold War, breaking through ideological barriers and divisions between the Eastern and Western blocs, Jin said. With the world again at crossroads, carrying that spirit forward is of renewed strategic significance, she said, adding that it can help shape whether countries pursue cooperation or confrontation, and whether the world slides into a new era of rival blocs. Bonne, the diplomatic adviser, who is visiting China from Friday to Tuesday, recalled Pompidou's visit as a memorable chapter in bilateral relations. France is willing to carry forward the long-standing friendship and continue developing a comprehensive strategic partnership based on mutual respect and trust, he said. Wang, who is also China's foreign minister, said the China-France Strategic Dialogue was the first high-level strategic consultation mechanism China established with a major Western country, noting its role in supporting diplomacy between the heads of state and consolidating political trust. The latest meeting followed French President Emmanuel Macron's fourth state visit to China in December last year. During that visit, the two leaders reached important common understandings on strengthening strategic communication, maintaining openness and cooperation, and jointly upholding multilateralism. Wang expressed the hope that France would provide policy support and a favorable environment for Chinese companies investing in the country. Bonne said that France would continue to offer Chinese investors a predictable business environment. On the Taiwan question, Wang urged France to honor its commitment to the one-China principle and safeguard the political foundation of bilateral relations. Bonne reaffirmed that commitment, saying that France's position would not change. Wang said that China and France, as major countries committed to independence and multilateralism, should strengthen communication within the United Nations framework and work toward a more just and equitable global governance system. Bonne expressed France's willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China to help the international community address global crises and achieve common development. The two sides also exchanged views on the Ukraine crisis and the situation in the Middle East, agreeing to maintain communication and coordination on international affairs. The dialogue followed the latest trade and investment consultations between China and the European Union in Beijing on Thursday and Friday, with both sides welcoming the progress made. Speaking to Bonne, Wang stressed that trust is a defining feature of China-EU relations and the foundation on which the ties rest, while economic and trade differences are temporary. The two sides should remain committed to their partnership and keep cooperation as the keynote of their relations, putting trade issues in their proper places within the broader relationship, he said. Bonne described the latest consultations as an important step in a positive direction, saying that Europe needs China for its development.

item.title: The Long March: An enduring inspiration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Retracing the Long March: From the birthplace of 25,000 Li to a new journey In August 1936, in response to Mao Zedong's call, Red Army soldiers put pen to paper to recount their firsthand experiences of the Long March (1934–36). Their accounts were compiled into a book titled 25,000 Li, which was completed in Yan'an in 1937. Ninety years after the victory of the Long March, China Daily reporter Yan An visits Yan'an, the cradle of the Chinese revolution and the place where the book was completed, to explore how the Long March has become a source of inspiration for generations to come. The Long March: An Enduring Inspiration, a mini-documentary that pays tribute to the enduring spirit of the Long March, premieres online on Oct 12. Follow Yan An as she retraces the footsteps of the Red Army and explores what the Long March spirit means for those embarking on their own new journeys today.

item.title: Xi on carrying forward Long March spirit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Xi on carrying forward Long March spirit Share - WeChat
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. President Xi Jinping has always stressed the importance of carrying forward the spirit of the Long March, which has become a powerful spiritual force inspiring the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and advance from victory to victory.
